title: Recruitment without discrimination: Brussels Code
summary: The Brussels Code of 2024 is the current reference within Brussels’s competence scope. Selection criteria must comply with anti-discrimination prohibitions and reasonable adjustment rules.
body: The joint decree and ordinance of April 4, 2024, published on April 16 and effective October 16, 2024, covers employment and employment relations within the competence limits specified in article 6. Articles 5 and 7 protect notably age, sex, origin, disability, language, family responsibilities, and health status. They prohibit direct, indirect, and intersectional discrimination, as well as instructions to discriminate.

To draft a job offer and compare applications, link each requirement to the position’s tasks. Articles 8, 10, 13, and 14 frame possible justifications, notably essential and determinative professional requirements, whose objective must be legitimate and the requirement proportionate.

Articles 11 and 12 require processing accommodation requests related to disability. A refusal must be justified when the accommodation would be unreasonable; a charge sufficiently compensated by public subsidies is not disproportionate. Article 203 repeals the September 4, 2008 ordinance on employment discrimination.
source: Brussels-Capital Region, COCOM and COCOF · ejustice.just.fgov.be

owner.name: Région de Bruxelles-Capitale, COCOM et COCOF

title: Anti-discrimination ordinance of 2008: repealed text
summary: The September 4, 2008 ordinance on employment discrimination has been repealed. For a new job posting, use the Brussels Code of 2024.
body: The Justel record of the September 4, 2008 ordinance, published September 16, 2008, explicitly states that the text is repealed. This record helps identify old references still present in certain guides and internal documents.

Do not present the old articles as the current legal basis for recruitment. The Brussels Code of April 4, 2024 takes up the framework of equality and non-discrimination; its article 203 specifically targets the repeal of this ordinance.

title: Discrimination testing by Brussels inspection
summary: The inspection can use comparable applications and mystery calls to detect discrimination. The system established in 2017 was expanded in 2023.
body: Article 4/3 of the April 30, 2009 ordinance, inserted by the November 16, 2017 ordinance and modified in 2023, authorizes testing under assumed identity. Situation testing compares applications differing only by a potentially discriminatory criterion; mystery calls verify an employer’s reaction to a discriminatory request from a client.

In the version updated June 29, 2023, a complaint is no longer the only entry point. Paragraph 4 also allows testing based on reasonable suspicion from an investigation, social data, or sector analysis. Sector cases referenced in points c and d require prior express agreement from the labor auditor or the King’s Prosecutor. The test cannot provoke discrimination.

Actions and results are recorded in a report. A positive result may presume discrimination. The recruiter must apply consistent criteria to applications and refuse discriminatory instruction, including when it comes from a client.

title: Language of personnel documents in Brussels
summary: In Brussels, individual documents covered by law are drafted in French for French-speaking staff and Dutch for Dutch-speaking staff. The region’s bilingualism does not require two versions of each individual document.
body: Article 52 of the coordinated laws of July 18, 1966 regulates acts and documents legally required and those intended for staff of industrial, commercial, or financial enterprises. The territorial criterion is the place of business. In Brussels-Capital, choose French or Dutch according to the language of the staff member concerned.

For a collective document intended for French-speaking and Dutch-speaking staff, provide both versions. Article 52, paragraph 2, allows adding a translation to notices, communications, acts, certificates, and forms when staff composition justifies it. A translation does not dispense with establishing the document in the legally required language.

According to article 59, an irregular document must be replaced spontaneously or upon notice. If not followed within a month, the justice of the peace can order the addition of a sworn translation at the company’s expense. The replacement takes effect on the date of the replaced document. Justel version updated May 9, 2016.

title: Activa.brussels: closure and transition in 2026
summary: Since July 15, 2026, activa.brussels no longer funds new hires. Actiris plans a transition for contracts already started, until December 31, 2026.
body: The notice to employers covers activa.brussels, activa.brussels plus, and activa.brussels reduced capacity. For a recruitment performed after the July 15, 2026 closure, do not deduct an activa allowance from the projected salary cost.

Actiris clarifies that the deduction continues for contracts started before July 15, 2026, until December 31, 2026. As of January 1, 2027, the employer must bear the full salary without this deduction. Verify the effective contract start date in transitional files.

The disability bonus and training incentive are no longer available. Programs such as Stage First or FPIE no longer provide access to an activa certificate. The page announces work on replacement measures without yet setting their conditions.

title: Activa: amounts and transitional file declaration
summary: DRS instructions for the third quarter of 2026 indicate maximum amounts of Brussels allowances and their calculation. Their use assumes a right still open during activa transition.
body: For period 2026/3, scenario 8 table indicates 350 or 800 euros for type 020, long-term unemployed Brussels residents, and 600 or 750 euros for type 021, reduced capacity and target group of youth or older workers. Apply the amount corresponding to the granting decision and file stage, without promising these amounts for a new hire.

Calculation is done per declared occupation based on remunerated hours and factor S multiplied by four. Add calculated amounts to determine the monthly deduction, then respect the applicable ceiling when deducting net salary. Instructions distinguish this capping from the amount to declare.

Read these instructions with the bruxelles-activa-abrogation-transition-2026 fact sheet: new hires have been excluded since July 15, 2026 and the transitional deduction ends December 31, 2026. The date used corresponds to the start of the third quarter 2026 covered by the instructions.

title: Publish and track a job offer on My Actiris
summary: Actiris terms of use require genuine job offers, accurate descriptions, and application tracking. Services are free and the employer remains responsible for published content.
body: Terms updated June 26, 2024 require a VAT number and compliance with employer’s legal obligations. According to article 1, self-managed job offers can be published in French, Dutch, or English; those managed by Actiris are drafted in French and/or Dutch, with a separate framework for international.

Articles 2 and 3 require publishing only positions actually to be filled, describing work precisely, and respecting notably CBA no. 38 and anti-discrimination rules. Follow applications within a reasonable timeframe and close expired offers. In Actiris management, also communicate the outcome of proposed applications.

Article 4 reserves candidate data for the recruitment procedure and prohibits their communication to third parties. Actiris can suspend an offer and block an account for non-compliance with conditions, per article 5.

title: Stage First: conditions and allowances in 2026
summary: Stage First is a first professional experience internship governed by an agreement with Actiris. Since March 27, 2026, the minimum prior enrollment required by the text is 26 days.
body: Article 4 of the September 29, 2016 order, amended in March 2026, requires less than 30 years at the internship start, at most a secondary education diploma or certificate, a Brussels residence, and at least 26 days of registration as an unemployed job seeker with Actiris. Have eligibility verified before concluding the agreement.

Articles 2, 3, 5, and 6 provide for an agreement between trainee, training provider, and Actiris, accompanied by a support plan. The internship lasts 3 to 6 months and follows the full-time regime applicable to the function in the sector. It should not be presented as an ordinary employment contract.

Articles 11 and 12 set a daily allowance of 26.82 euros and a monthly indemnity of 500 euros charged to the provider. The 500-euro amount applies to agreements concluded since July 1, 2024. Before starting, subscribe to work accident insurance, commute insurance, and civil liability insurance under article 9; establish the final evaluation required by article 10.

title: Work authorization: submission to single window
summary: Check the applicant’s residence status and category before requesting a Brussels authorization. Since May 4, 2026, applications for non-EU nationals go through the federal single window.
body: Brussels Economy and Employment offers guidance by situation: highly qualified worker, shortage profession, blue card, trainee, seasonal work, or other case. Use the category actually corresponding to the job and check any exemptions and applicable minimum compensation.
As of May 4, 2026, PDF forms are no longer used and email requests are no longer accepted. If a proxy is involved, the employer and proxy must follow the power of attorney procedure.

A work authorization issued by the Region does not automatically constitute a single permit. The residence decision falls under the Office of Foreign Affairs, per articles 61/25-1 et seq. of the December 15, 1980 law. Holders of special residence status must provide proof of waiver of their privileged status.

title: Shortage profession: choose work authorization
summary: Classification as a shortage profession does not exempt from requesting appropriate authorization. Brussels distinguishes work duration and whether or not residing in Belgium.
body: The official page refers to the shortage professions list published July 1, 2026 and article 14, paragraph 2, 1°, of the May 16, 2024 order. Compare job tasks and position title with this list before using the corresponding economic migration category.

For more than 90 days of work with residence in Belgium, request a single permit. For more than 90 days without residence in Belgium, notably the stated cross-border or remote work case outside Belgium, the page directs to long-duration authorization. Up to 90 days, it directs to short-duration authorization; successive occupations are counted in this calculation.

title: Shortage professions: list of July 1, 2026
summary: The list distributed by Brussels Economy and Employment identifies shortage professions as of July 1, 2026. Verify the exact title before preparing an economic migration file.
body: The list includes notably accountant, chartered accountant, construction manager, construction equipment operator, mason, sloped roof roofer, and flat roof roofer. In care and social action are notably care assistant, nurse, and educator-companion.

For IT, the document notably covers ICT analyst-developer, ICT Business Analyst, and database administrator. In hospitality, it mentions chef; in transport, heavy goods driver with CE license. A similar title or entire sector is therefore insufficient to establish list membership.

Keep the July 1, 2026 version with the recruitment file and verify correspondence with the actual function. For procedures related to the foreign candidate, then use the procedure indicated in the bruxelles-profession-penurie-autorisation fact sheet.

title: Critical functions: adapt recruitment requirements
summary: Critical functions correspond to recruitment difficulties that can have multiple causes. Actiris invites examining requested qualifications and training opportunities.
body: The Actiris Panorama page, updated July 10, 2026, explains that education, experience, language, or flexibility requirements can reduce the number of available candidates. To prepare a job offer, distinguish skills needed from the start from those that can be acquired on the job.

Actiris cites returning to education, training, and skills validation among pathways to occupations that are hiring. Use job fact sheets to prepare candidate search; the absence of a function in this selection does not mean no opportunities exist.

title: PHARE: insertion bonus for a disabled worker
summary: The PHARE insertion bonus can compensate for productivity loss related to disability. The request is joint between the worker and employer and requires a service decision.
body: Articles 71 to 78 of the May 7, 2015 COCOF order frame this assistance. For a worker covered by the PHARE system, assistance covers gross compensation increased by employer contributions; base compensation is capped at three times the guaranteed average minimum monthly income. The rules presented appear in the consolidated text as of February 19, 2024.

For an open-ended or fixed-term contract of more than three months, the rate depends on the assessed productivity loss and cannot exceed 50%. Granting is limited to one year, renewable if the loss persists. For a contract of three months or less, the rate is 30%, with a limit of six months’ assistance per year with the same employer.

Have both parties sign the request and provide performance records, payslips, and NSSO declarations. Article 72 excludes notably double interventions intended to compensate for the same productivity loss and certain public employers not meeting their mandatory quota.
source: French-speaking Community Commission / PHARE Service · ejustice.just.fgov.be

title: Diversity plan: financing and Actiris label
summary: The employer can have a diversity plan approved with Actiris and request financing. The label requires favorable evaluation of a global or thematic plan.
body: Articles 7 and 8 of the May 7, 2009 order provide for a lead structure, involvement of competent consultation bodies, and support by an Actiris diversity consultant. The file notably analyzes recruitment, personnel management, internal communication, and external positioning, then sets objectives and a timeline.

In the regime effective January 1, 2020, article 9 caps the mini-plan at 5,000 euros. The global plan and thematic plan can receive maximum co-financing of 10,000 euros covering at most half of eligible expenses. The maximum period is 24 months, subject to available funding; ordinary worker salaries are not eligible.

Articles 11 and 14 condition payment on justifications, activity report, and favorable evaluation. Article 15 then allows requesting the label for sites covered by a global or thematic plan. Do not announce label achievement upon plan submission.
